title: Length bound for a visit row
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Booleans, let $C,e,x$ be natural-number parameters and a Boolean word, and let $t,N$ be natural numbers with $t\le N$. The visit row for $x$ and the unary time word of length $t$ has length at most $k(2N+6)$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes of $M$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
replaced: For every source machine, parameters $C$ and $e$, instance $x$, and times $t \le N$, the packed visit row at time $t$ has length at most $k(2N + 6)$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes; a delimiter is stored even for an absent visit.
